title: Day 3 PSM — Section 2
subject: Community Medicine
description: FMGE Community Medicine practice from the reviewed Day 3 PSM question bank, section 2 of 4.

questions.stem: The red Anemia Mukt Bharat tablet for pregnant women contains how much elemental iron?
questions.explanation: The red tablet contains 60 mg elemental iron and 500 µg folic acid.

questions.stem: A woman has a positive VIA screening result. Which procedure can establish the cervical diagnosis?
questions.explanation: VIA and cytology are screening procedures. A colposcopically directed punch biopsy provides diagnostic tissue.

questions.stem: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first:
questions.explanation: Infants should receive only breast milk for the first six months, apart from permitted medical supplements or treatment.

questions.stem: ICDS services are delivered locally through the:
questions.explanation: Anganwadi centres deliver ICDS services to mothers and children.

questions.stem: Which skin finding is a clinical clue to leprosy?
questions.explanation: A skin patch with reduced sensation is an important clinical clue to leprosy.

questions.stem: Well water remains hard after boiling. Which process can soften it?
questions.explanation: Hardness that persists after boiling is permanent hardness from sulphates and chlorides. The permutit (base-exchange) process removes it.

questions.stem: A test gives 60 true-negative and 20 false-negative results. Its negative predictive value is:
questions.explanation: Negative predictive value is TN/(TN + FN), so it is 60/80, or 75%.

questions.stem: GeneXpert MTB/RIF can detect tuberculosis and resistance to:
questions.explanation: GeneXpert MTB/RIF detects *M. tuberculosis* and rifampicin resistance.

questions.stem: Comparison of a test with a gold standard assesses its:
questions.explanation: Criterion validity is assessed by comparing the test against a gold standard.

questions.stem: The principal disinfecting form of free chlorine in water is:
questions.explanation: Hypochlorous acid provides the main disinfecting action of free chlorine.

questions.stem: A clinic visitor is offered a screening test during an unrelated appointment. This is:
questions.explanation: Screening offered because a person is already in contact with a service is opportunistic screening.

questions.stem: The instrument shown measures which environmental parameter?
questions.image_alt: Handheld frame with two slender instruments mounted side by side
questions.image_source: p.114 | lower-right photograph of the handheld rotating instrument; crop out the written heading and answer
questions.explanation: The pictured sling psychrometer measures air humidity.

questions.stem: Which organism serves as a biological indicator of air pollution?
questions.explanation: Lichens are biological indicators of air pollution.

questions.stem: Liquid chemical biomedical waste requires which step before discharge?
questions.explanation: Liquid chemical biomedical waste is treated before it enters the drain.

questions.stem: The principal indicator of faecal contamination of drinking water is:
questions.explanation: *E. coli* is the principal indicator of faecal contamination in drinking water.

questions.stem: The preferred method for disposal of municipal refuse is:
questions.explanation: Sanitary landfill (controlled tipping) is the preferred method of refuse disposal.

questions.stem: A programme targets the larvae of mosquitoes transmitting malaria. Which biological control agent is used?
questions.explanation: *Anopheles* transmits malaria, and Gambusia fish eat its larvae. DDT, pyrethrum and malathion are chemical controls.

questions.stem: The vector of kala-azar is the:
questions.explanation: Sandflies transmit kala-azar.

questions.stem: Solidification with cement and lime is used for large quantities of toxic biomedical waste. The process is:
questions.explanation: Inertization incorporates toxic waste into a solid mixture using cement and lime.

questions.stem: A healthy infant’s length is approximately how much at the end of the first year?
questions.explanation: Infant length rises from about 50 cm at birth to about 75 cm by one year.

questions.stem: Under Anganwadi supplementary nutrition norms, the daily energy allocation for a severely malnourished child aged 6–72 months is:
questions.explanation: A severely malnourished child aged 6–72 months receives 800 kcal daily under Anganwadi supplementary nutrition.

questions.stem: All of the following describe green disaster triage EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Green identifies ambulatory casualties with minor injuries. Immediate resuscitation places a casualty in a higher-priority category.

questions.stem: Microwave treatment of biomedical waste operates at a frequency of:
questions.explanation: Biomedical-waste microwave treatment operates at 2,450 MHz.

questions.stem: Solid waste originating from a household kitchen is termed:
questions.explanation: Kitchen-origin solid waste is termed garbage.

questions.stem: The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed on:
questions.explanation: The International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction is observed on 13 October.

questions.stem: During war, minor injuries are given priority so personnel can return to duty. This is:
questions.explanation: Reverse triage can prioritize personnel with minor injuries for prompt return to duty.

questions.stem: Direct rupture of the tympanic membrane by a sudden noise occurs at about:
questions.explanation: A sudden noise of about 150–160 dB can rupture the tympanic membrane. Auditory fatigue begins around 90 dB.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy has a mental age of 9 years. He is best classified as having:
questions.explanation: IQ \(=9/15\times100=60\), which lies in the mild band of 50–69.

questions.stem: The maximum number of students recommended per classroom is:
questions.explanation: A classroom should hold no more than 40 students.

questions.stem: After the Chernobyl accident, the radionuclide chiefly responsible for the rise in childhood thyroid cancer was:
questions.explanation: Radioactive iodine-131 concentrates in the thyroid. Childhood exposure after Chernobyl increased thyroid cancer.

questions.stem: Under the persons-per-room overcrowding criterion, three rooms accommodate at most:
questions.explanation: The persons-per-room table allows up to five people in a three-room dwelling.

questions.stem: The standard population screening test for breast cancer in average-risk women aged 50–69 years is:
questions.explanation: Mammography is the standard population screening test for breast cancer. FNAC and biopsy are used for diagnosis.
